package_info.package_manager: Phishing-as-a-Service (PaaS) platform (not a traditional package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (service-based, not versioned in the traditional sense)
package_info.why_malicious: EvilProxy is a malicious phishing toolkit that leverages reverse proxy techniques to intercept and steal multi-factor authentication (MFA)-protected credentials and session cookies, enabling adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) attacks and persistent account takeover (ATO) against high-value targets.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
From: autonotification@concursolutions[.]com
From: dse@eumail.docusign[.]net
From: adobesign@adobesign[.]com
Subject: [Impersonated brand notification]
Body: [HTML with embedded link to open redirector or malicious domain]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon email delivery, the code impersonates trusted brands and embeds links to open redirectors or malicious domains, luring the victim to click and initiate the phishing chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Brand impersonation in unsolicited emails is a classic phishing tactic, especially when combined with links to non-canonical domains.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate brand notifications should originate from official domains and not redirect users to suspicious or unrelated domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate brands may send notifications, but always from official domains and with verifiable links.
key_indicators: Embedded links to open redirectors or non-brand domains

execution_context.file_location: phishing email (embedded URL), open redirector (e.g., YouTube redirect), malicious domain

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user clicks the phishing link, the browser is redirected via a legitimate open redirector (e.g., YouTube) to a malicious domain controlled by the attacker, evading security scanning and increasing user trust.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of open redirectors to funnel users to malicious domains is a known evasion and social engineering technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate links should not use open redirectors to reach authentication pages.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Open redirectors are sometimes used for tracking or marketing, but not for authentication workflows.
key_indicators: Use of open redirectors (e.g., YouTube) in authentication flows

execution_context.file_location: malicious web server (reverse proxy code, JavaScript, server-side logic)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the reverse proxy intercepts all traffic between the victim and the legitimate authentication provider, capturing credentials, MFA tokens, and session cookies, then relays them to the attacker while presenting a seamless login experience to the victim.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting authentication flows and session cookies is a hallmark of adversary-in-the-middle phishing attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate authentication pages do not proxy or intercept user credentials or session cookies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Reverse proxies are used for load balancing or security, but not for credential interception.

execution_context.trigger: user submits credentials and completes MFA

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon successful credential and MFA submission, the code captures the session cookie and uses it to establish a session with the legitimate service, bypassing MFA and enabling account takeover.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Capturing and reusing session cookies to bypass MFA is a direct violation of authentication security.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Session cookies should never be accessible to third parties or reused outside the original browser context.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Session management is legitimate, but not in the context of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After account takeover, the attacker adds their own multi-factor authentication method to the compromised account, establishing persistent access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Adding a new MFA method without user consent is a strong indicator of account compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: MFA enrollment should only occur with explicit user action and notification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Users may add MFA methods, but not from suspicious sessions or locations.
key_indicators: MFA method enrollment from new device/location

attack_chain.action: Phishing email impersonates a trusted brand and delivers a malicious link to the target.
attack_chain.leads_to: User clicks the link, initiating the redirect chain.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the link, which uses an open redirector to funnel the victim to a malicious domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim lands on the attacker-controlled phishing page.

attack_chain.action: Malicious phishing page (reverse proxy) intercepts all authentication traffic, capturing credentials, MFA tokens, and session cookies.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives credentials and session data.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses captured session cookie to establish a session with the legitimate service, bypassing MFA and taking over the account.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent access to the victim's account.

attack_chain.action: Attacker adds their own MFA method to the compromised account, ensuring continued access.

behavioral_signatures: Phishing emails impersonating trusted brands with links to open redirectors or non-canonical domains
User authentication flows proxied through non-official domains
Session cookie and credential interception by reverse proxy
Unusual MFA method enrollment from new devices or locations
file_indicators: URLs containing open redirector patterns (e.g., youtube.com/redirect)
Domains such as concurcloud[.]us, concursolutions[.]info, etc.
network_indicators: Connections to known EvilProxy infrastructure IPs (e.g., 154.29.75.192, 185.241.52.78, etc.)
HTTP requests to malicious 'Step 2' redirection domains (see IOC list)
Unusual authentication traffic patterns (e.g., login from new IP, session replay)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for phishing emails impersonating trusted brands with links to open redirectors or suspicious domains. Detect authentication flows that are proxied through non-official domains, especially those that capture session cookies or credentials. Alert on new MFA method enrollments from unusual devices or locations, and correlate with known EvilProxy infrastructure IPs and domains. Use threat intelligence feeds to block or flag connections to listed IOCs.
